newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool test for sale rises July/Jan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool test for sale rises July/Jan.

text.p: The weight of Australian wool tested for sale in the first seven months of the 1996/97 season rose by 3.6 percent nationally, the Australian Wool Testing Authority Ltd (AWTA) said on Tuesday.
The AWTA said it tested 2.47 million bales in the July to January period against 2.37 million bales a year earlier.
A larger proportion of the clip was tested for length and strength, with 75.3 percent of the clip measured in July to January 1996/97 against 71.9 percent a year earlier.
Overall yields were marginally higher, vegetable matter content slightly heavier, but average fibre diameter the same at 21.9 microns, the AWTA said.
Staple length was marginally lower but staple strength was slightly better, it said.
There was also a greater quantity of superfine wool in the clip, with the number of bales of superfine wool of 19.5 microns and finer rising by almost 62,000 bales, it said.
It gave no figures for the superfine total.
